overview: Systems keep arriving from the Pacific through the holiday, favoring the Cascades and Montana first, then Colorado and Wyoming on Friday and Saturday. Coastal regions stay wet and mild into the weekend.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A series of disturbances keeps rain and wind going through Thursday, with snow levels high, so most falls as rain except on the upper mountain. Crystal Mountain leads the region with a 37" total, and Thursday is its biggest day at 13". The NWS is calling for more, 21 to 32 inches Saturday night through Monday, though it is unsure of timing.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving with fog in the valleys. A Pacific system brings wind along the Rocky Mountain Front, then snow to the Continental Divide from Friday into Saturday. Grand Targhee tops the region at 42", with its best day Saturday at 24".

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Rain dominates Wednesday and Thursday, with snow only at the top of the mountains. Whistler's 32" total is mostly from its early-week rain-and-snow run, and conditions turn showery and mixed through the weekend.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A weak front brings light rain and a dusting of snow by Wednesday, then dry weather returns. Sugar Bowl and Palisades both look to get 18" on Sunday as a wetter system arrives, with rain mixing with snow.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Showers and rain dominate Wednesday through Thursday, with a snow level near 1000 metres. Snow picks up again Sunday as cooler air arrives. Whitewater leads with 17", most of it on Thursday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild, dry weather continues through Thanksgiving, with patchy valley fog Wednesday. A system moves in from Friday into Saturday, with the heaviest snow in the Park Range and forecasters unsure how far south it reaches. Steamboat leads at 16", with its best day Saturday at 12".

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers arrive Wednesday night and Thursday, then conditions turn drier and partly sunny Friday and Saturday. Big White has the best total at 10", most of it falling Thursday.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Mixed snow and rain runs Thursday and Friday, with a special weather statement for Friday into Saturday in Quebec. Le Massif leads at 8", with snow and rain showers continuing through Sunday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
